# Joe’s Vintage Guitars — Internal Linking & On-Page Enrichment Plan

Covers: contextual internal links (priority targets = serial guides, sell pages, /free-appraisal/), section-level related posts, FAQ gaps, relevant reviews/videos/social per section, schema.org Dataset markup, and DB fact flags.

# Social Embed Candidates — Joe's Vintage Guitars

Fresh scrape: 2026-06-22 via Apify (Instagram, YouTube, Facebook, Pinterest). TikTok and Reverb could not be scraped — see NEEDS JOSH at bottom.

## Embed-Type Support (Reference)

| Platform | Official oEmbed/Embed? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| YouTube | YES — official `<iframe>` embed | Most reliable. Both long videos and Shorts embed via `/embed/<id>`. **Best embed target.** |
| Instagram | YES — official oEmbed (`/embed`) | Requires the Instagram embed script (`//www.instagram.com/embed.js`) or a Facebook Graph API token for oEmbed since 2020. Reels and image posts both embeddable. |
| TikTok | YES — official oEmbed + blockquote+`embed.js` | Standard `<blockquote class="tiktok-embed">`. But see NEEDS JOSH (profile not found). |
| Pinterest | PARTIAL — pin/board/profile widgets via `pinit.js` | No true oEmbed; uses Pinterest widget builder data attributes. Works but heavier; pins here are SEO promo graphics, low embed value. |
| Facebook | PARTIAL — official Page/Post embed via SDK (`fb-root` + `sdk.js`) | Requires the FB JS SDK. Reels embed inconsistently; Page-post embeds are more reliable than Reel embeds. FB content here largely duplicates Instagram Reels — prefer the IG/YT version of the same guitar. |

**Recommendation:** prioritize **YouTube** embeds (cleanest, no token) and **Instagram Reels** (strong storytelling captions) for the guides/value/sell pages. Use Facebook/Pinterest only where no IG/YT equivalent exists.

# Dataset JSON-LD for Joe's Reference Tables

Recommendation pass for adding schema.org `Dataset` markup to the serial / value / spec tables across the Archetype B reference pages. Josh wants more `Dataset` coverage; this section says which tables qualify, gives a concrete block to copy, shows the Astro wiring, and lays out the SEO/AEO rationale.

Cross-checked against `reports/seo/_sections/_db-fact-index.txt` (VG-0001..VG-0112). Where a table's framing touches a verified fact, the VG id is cited inline.

---

## 1. Which tables are genuine "datasets" worth Dataset markup

A `Dataset` should describe a structured, downloadable-in-spirit collection of observations: a serial-range-to-year lookup, a price matrix, a spec timeline. A table that is mostly prose with a couple of year columns is borderline; a true range-to-value or code-to-year lookup is the real thing. Tier them:

### Tier 1 — Strong datasets (mark these)

These are clean lookup tables: a key (serial range / code / year) maps to a value (year / price / spec). They read like reference data, which is exactly what `Dataset` is for, and they are the tables most likely to be cited by an AI assistant answering "what year is Fender serial L12345."

| Page | Table(s) | Why it qualifies | Fact cross-check |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fender-guitars-serial-number-guide.astro` | Bridge-plate (1950–1954), 4/5-digit neck plate (1954–1963), L-Series (1963–1965), F-plate 6-digit (1965–1976), V-prefix, Custom Shop CN/CZ/R, headstock decade-letter (1976–present), Mexican (M-prefix), Made-in-Japan, Crafted-in-Japan | Range→year(s)→era lookups, the canonical "serial decoder" data | Ranges overlap / "no earlier than" caveat is real: VG-0050, VG-0053, VG-0060, VG-0061, VG-0062. Decade letters S/E/N: VG-0063. JV/MIJ/CIJ reuse: VG-0064. Mexico MN/MZ/MX: VG-0065. L-series 1963–65: VG-0067. F-plate CBS: VG-0068. |
| `how-to-read-gibson-serial-numbers.astro` | FON tables (1902–1945, banner era), white-label (1902–1947), A-prefix (1947–1961), ink-stamp solid-body (1952–1960), 1961–1970 reused-number ranges, Norlin-era, modern 8/9-digit YDDDYRRR | Range→year lookups; the 1961–69 overlap table is itself a dataset of documented collisions | 1961–69 unreliable / overlap: VG-0011, VG-0013, VG-0031, VG-0036 (100000–106099 spans 1963 + 1967). FON year-letter A–H: VG-0034. Modern YDDDYRRR: VG-0035, VG-0016. |
| `vintage-fender-amplifier-serial-numbers-how-to-find-the-year.astro` | Tube-chart two-letter date-code table (A=1951 … T=1970, the `tubeChartCodes` array) | Letter→year lookup, the cleanest dataset on the site | Amps not datable by serial, tube chart is the method: VG-0052. |
| `vintage-gibson-les-paul-market-value-guide.astro` | "Vintage Les Paul Values by Model and Year" (`prices[]`, 12 rows of model+year → price range) | Model/year → USD range matrix | Burst $200k–500k+ and 1.5k–1.7k made: VG-0028, VG-0029, VG-0030. Refin ~−40 to 50%: VG-0074, VG-0107. |
| `vintage-fender-stratocaster-value-guide.astro` | "Vintage Stratocaster Values (1954 to 1965)" (Year → Sunburst → Custom Color) | Year → price-by-finish matrix | Custom-color premium / refin penalty: VG-0058, VG-0073, VG-0074. |
| `vintage-fender-telecaster-value-guide.astro` | Value-by-year/finish table | Same shape as Strat guide | Blackguard 1950–mid-54: VG-0069. |
| `martin-d-28-d-18-d-45-dreadnought-value-guide.astro` | Value table(s) for D-28/D-18/D-45 by era | Model/era → price matrix | Herringbone/scalloped pre-war premium: VG-0080. D-45 1942–1968 gap: VG-0081. Herringbone discontinued 1947: VG-0085, VG-0087. Brazilian→Indian rosewood 1969: VG-0088, VG-0089, VG-0109. |

### Tier 2 — Spec timelines (defensible as Dataset, one per page is enough)

The Gibson page's model "Dating by Model and Features" tables (Les Paul / SG / ES-335 finish-by-year, pickup-by-year, hardware-by-year, era spec grids) are spec timelines: feature → year-range → notes. Each one individually is thin, but the **collection** of them per model is a legitimate spec dataset. Recommendation: do NOT mark each little 4-row table; instead emit **one `Dataset` per model section** (e.g. "Gibson Les Paul dating-by-feature dataset") whose `variableMeasured` lists Finish, Pickups, Hardware, Body style, etc., and whose `temporalCoverage` spans the model's run. Same approach for the Fender SN page's "Model-Specific Dating Guides" and "Logo Evolution" timelines.

### Not datasets (skip)

- The condition-grading tables on `/free-appraisal/` — those are a rubric/definition list, not observational data.
- Authentication checklists, "Joe's Tip" callouts, FAQ accordions (already covered by `FAQPage`).
- Single-row or two-cell "comparison" tables (ES-335 vs ES-345 feature table) — too small to be a meaningful Dataset; leave as plain `<table>`.

**Shipping order:** the 10 Fender SN serial tables + the Gibson serial tables + the amp tube-chart table are the highest-value Tier 1 targets (highest query volume, cleanest data, best AI-citation payoff). Do those first; value-guide price matrices second; spec timelines last.

---

## 2. Concrete example: Dataset JSON-LD for one serial table

Below is a ready-to-adapt block for the **Fender L-Series serial table** (`#l-series` on the Fender SN guide). It names Joe as `creator` via his canonical `@id`, points `license` at the permissive photo-license terms already in `site.ts`, declares the measured variables, the year span, and topical keywords.

```js
const lSeriesDataset = {
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Dataset",
  "@id": "https://www.joesvintageguitarsaz.com/fender-guitars-serial-number-guide/#l-series-dataset",
  name: "Fender L-Series Serial Number to Year Lookup (1963 to 1965)",
  description:
    "Serial-number-range to production-year reference for Fender L-prefix neck-plate guitars, covering the final pre-CBS hand-built years through the early CBS transition. Note that Fender pre-stamped neck plates in batches, so a single serial can span two or three years; values give the documented year range, not a single guaranteed year.",
  url: "https://www.joesvintageguitarsaz.com/fender-guitars-serial-number-guide/#l-series",
  isPartOf: {
    "@id": "https://www.joesvintageguitarsaz.com/fender-guitars-serial-number-guide/",
  },
  creator: { "@id": "https://www.joesvintageguitarsaz.com/about-me/#person" },
  publisher: { "@id": "https://www.joesvintageguitarsaz.com/" },
  // Permissive terms already defined in src/config/site.ts (imageLicense.photoLicenseUrl)
  license: "https://www.joesvintageguitarsaz.com/photo-license/",
  isAccessibleForFree: true,
  inLanguage: "en-US",
  temporalCoverage: "1963/1965",
  keywords: [
    "Fender serial numbers",
    "L-series Fender",
    "pre-CBS Fender",
    "vintage Fender dating",
    "Fender neck plate serial",
  ],
  variableMeasured: [
    { "@type": "PropertyValue", name: "Serial number range", description: "L-prefix neck-plate serial range" },
    { "@type": "PropertyValue", name: "Production year(s)", description: "Documented year or year span for the range" },
    { "@type": "PropertyValue", name: "Era", description: "Pre-CBS, Transition, or CBS" },
  ],
};
```

Notes on the field choices:

- **`creator` = Joe's `@id`** reuses `https://www.joesvintageguitarsaz.com/about-me/#person`, the same node every Article on these pages already references (verified in the amp + Les Paul page source). Do not redefine the Person inline; just point at it.
- **`license`** uses the permissive photo-license URL (`imageLicense.photoLicenseUrl` in `site.ts`). Joe authored this reference data and wants reuse-with-credit, matching the content-photo tier. Do NOT use the restrictive brand-assets URL here.
- **`temporalCoverage`** uses ISO interval `1963/1965`. For "to present" tables use an open interval, e.g. `"1976/.."`; for the tube-chart table use `"1951/1970"`.
- **`variableMeasured`** mirrors the table's `<thead>` columns exactly (Serial Range / Year(s) / Era), which is what makes Google read it as a real dataset.
- **`@id` with a `#...-dataset` fragment** keeps each table's Dataset node uniquely addressable and lets `isPartOf` tie it to the page.

For a **price matrix** (e.g. Strat value guide) the shape is the same but `variableMeasured` becomes `[Year, Sunburst value (USD), Custom Color value (USD)]`, `temporalCoverage` is `"1954/1965"`, and add `measurementTechnique: "Completed-sale market analysis"` plus a `dateModified` matching the "Updated March 2026" note in the table. Keep prices framed as ranges (the page already does), consistent with VG-0108 (Reverb price-guide values are estimates from completed sales) and VG-0112 (originality is the dominant value driver).

---

## 3. Wiring it into the Astro Layout `structuredData` prop

`Layout.astro` already accepts `structuredData?: Record<string, unknown> | Record<string, unknown>[]` (line 25) and spreads arrays into the page's `<head>` JSON-LD (lines 207–209). Every reference page already passes an array (`structuredData={[breadcrumbSchema, articleSchema, ...]}` on the Fender page; a mutated `structuredData[]` on the Les Paul page). So adding a Dataset is purely additive — no Layout change needed.

**Pattern A — pages with an inline `structuredData` array** (Fender SN guide, amp page):

```astro
---
// ...existing breadcrumb/article/faq/tool schemas...

const lSeriesDataset = { /* block from section 2 */ };
const bridgePlateDataset = { /* same shape, temporalCoverage "1950/1954" */ };
// ...one per Tier-1 table...
---
<Layout
  ...
  structuredData={[
    articleSchema, breadcrumbSchema, faqSchema, toolSchema, webPageSchema, ogImageSchema,
    lSeriesDataset, bridgePlateDataset, /* ...the rest... */
  ]}
>
```

**Pattern B — pages that `push()` onto a `structuredData` array** (Les Paul value guide already does `structuredData.push(faqSchema)`):

```astro
const valuesDataset = { /* Dataset block, variableMeasured = Model & Year, Value */ };
structuredData.push(valuesDataset);
```

**Keep the data DRY.** The tables are already driven by typed arrays (`neckPlateRows`, `lSeriesRows`, `tubeChartCodes`, `prices`, etc.). Build the Dataset's static metadata by hand (name/description/keywords/variableMeasured), but if you ever want to publish the rows themselves as machine-readable data, you can add a `distribution` with an inline data URL generated from the same array, so the `<table>` and the Dataset never drift:

```js
distribution: [{
  "@type": "DataDownload",
  encodingFormat: "text/csv",
  contentUrl:
    "data:text/csv;charset=utf-8," +
    encodeURIComponent(
      "Serial Range,Year(s),Era\n" +
      lSeriesRows.map((r) => r.join(",")).join("\n")
    ),
}],
```

This is optional; `variableMeasured` + `temporalCoverage` alone is enough for the rich result. The `distribution` mainly helps AI agents that want the raw rows.

**Helper suggestion (optional, reduces boilerplate across 20+ tables):** add a small `buildTableDataset({ id, name, description, anchor, columns, temporalCoverage, keywords })` to `src/lib/` that returns the node with `creator`/`publisher`/`license`/`isPartOf` filled in from `site.ts` (reuse `imageLicense.photoLicenseUrl` and the `#person` `@id`). Each page then calls it once per Tier-1 table instead of hand-writing the full block. Mirrors the existing `buildImageGraph()` pattern in `src/lib/imageLicense.ts`.

**Gate:** after adding, run the page through Google's Rich Results Test and confirm the **Dataset** item parses with 0 errors, and `npm run audit:live-diff` still shows 0 new 🔴 (JSON-LD parity check counts schema types). Dataset rich results are also previewable in Google's Dataset Search.

---

## 4. SEO / AEO rationale

**Google Dataset rich results + Dataset Search.** `Dataset` is one of Google's supported structured-data types; valid markup makes the page eligible for the Dataset rich result and for indexing in [Google Dataset Search](https://datasetsearch.research.google.com/). Serial-number-by-year lookups, price matrices, and spec timelines are exactly the "structured reference data" Dataset Search exists to surface. Almost no competing vintage-guitar site marks these tables up, so this is uncontested SERP real estate for queries like "fender serial number chart" or "les paul value by year."

**AI-citation / AEO.** This is the bigger win. When an assistant (ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, AI Overviews) answers "what's a 1959 Les Paul Standard worth" or "what year is Fender serial L25000," it preferentially grounds on clearly-structured, clearly-attributed data. A `Dataset` node with explicit `creator` (Joe, a named expert with a `#person` E-E-A-T node), `temporalCoverage`, `variableMeasured`, and `license` tells the model: this is curated reference data from an identifiable authority, safe to cite. That maps directly onto the site's existing AEO posture (the WebApplication decoder schema, the author E-E-A-T cards) and turns each table into an independently-citable unit.

**E-E-A-T reinforcement.** Pointing every Dataset's `creator` at the same `/about-me/#person` `@id` compounds the authorship signal already carried by the Article and decoder schemas: one expert, attributed across the decoder tool, the article body, the photos (via the image-license graph), and now the data tables. That consistency is what search and answer engines reward.

**Honesty guardrail (carry into the descriptions).** The serial datasets must not over-promise single-year precision: ranges overlap and serials give a "no earlier than" floor, not an exact date (VG-0050, VG-0053, VG-0060, VG-0061, VG-0062; Gibson 1961–69 collisions VG-0011/0013/0031/0036; amps not serial-datable VG-0052). Bake that caveat into each `description` (the example block does). Price datasets should stay range-based and note they are estimates from completed sales, not quotes (VG-0108), with originality flagged as the dominant driver (VG-0112). This keeps the markup truthful and matches the visible table copy, which is also what protects against a "misleading structured data" manual action.

---

## Quick build checklist

1. Add one `Dataset` node per Tier-1 table on: Fender SN guide (10 tables), Gibson SN guide (serial tables), amp page (tube-chart), Les Paul / Strat / Tele / Martin value guides (price matrices).
2. Add one `Dataset` per **model spec-timeline group** (Tier 2) on the Gibson SN guide and Fender SN model-guides section.
3. Each node: `creator` = `#person` `@id`, `publisher` = site `@id`, `license` = `imageLicense.photoLicenseUrl`, `variableMeasured` = the table's column headers, `temporalCoverage` = ISO interval, `keywords` = topical terms, `isPartOf` = page URL, honest `description`.
4. Spread/`push` into the existing `structuredData` prop — no `Layout.astro` change.
5. Verify each page in Google Rich Results Test (Dataset, 0 errors) and re-run `npm run audit:live-diff`.

# Part 2 — Per-Page Recommendations


---

## fender-guitars-serial-number-guide

`src/pages/fender-guitars-serial-number-guide.astro` — Archetype B reference/SEO page, ~30,000px tall, 15 H2 sections + interactive decoder tool + author E-E-A-T block. GSC: 93 clicks / 11,646 impr / pos 8.9 (top-3 priority page per gsc.md §3). linkgraph.md shows **10 unique in-content out-links, 21 instances** — but on inspection almost every one is an **intra-page anchor** (`#adv-pot-codes`, `#logo-evolution`, `#auth-hardware`, etc.). The page is **near-zero on contextual links to OTHER site pages**: the only cross-page links in body copy are `/free-appraisal/` (intro callout), the two model-guide blog CTAs, the bottom resource/sell cards, the related-guides grid, and one `/sell-my-fender-guitar/` card. The whole authentication + advanced-dating + model-guide spine — thousands of words naming sell-able brands, the appraisal funnel, and sibling serial guides — passes equity only inward via anchors.

This page is also a **major LINK SOURCE**: it is one of the highest-traffic pages on the site and currently links to `/how-to-read-gibson-serial-numbers/` only once (related grid) and to `/sell-my-fender-guitar/` twice. It should be feeding its sibling serial guides and the appraisal page far more.

Density target for a page this long (~9,000+ words of body copy): the page can comfortably carry **18 to 26 cross-page in-content links** at ~1 per 350-450 words without looking stuffed (the rule-of-thumb 1/120-180 would allow far more, but reference tables and image galleries eat word count without offering natural anchor homes — keep links in the prose `<p>` and callout text). Vary anchors hard: "Fender serial number guide" is already over-used 14x site-wide and "free appraisal" variants dozens of times.

### 3. FAQ gaps

The page has a strong 12-Q `FAQPage` block already (covers pot codes, pre-CBS vs CBS, Blackguard, slab board, custom color, Custom Shop, MIJ/MIM value, modification detection, database gaps, value). Genuine gaps where the page's own content answers a likely query but no FAQ exists:

1. **Q: What year is my Fender if the serial number falls in two different ranges on the chart?**
   A: It can be either. Fender pre-stamped neck plates in batches and pulled them in no particular order, so a single serial number legitimately spans two or three production years. The neck heel date and pot codes resolve it. (Reinforces VG-0050 / VG-0060 / VG-0061 / VG-0062 / VG-0111 — already partly covered by the "overlap" FAQ but worth a serial-range-specific phrasing for "what year is fender serial" queries.)

2. **Q: How do I date a Fender V-prefix Vintage Reissue?** (§7 has no FAQ analogue)
   A: You can't date it from the serial — V-prefix numbers carry no year code. Date it by the neck heel stamp, pot codes, and 1980s-or-later hardware. It is a modern reissue, not a vintage original, and should never be priced as vintage. (Page already states this in §7; surfacing it as an FAQ captures "fender v serial number" queries.)

3. **Q: What do the S, E, N, Z, and US letter prefixes on a Fender headstock mean?** (§9 formula has no FAQ)
   A: They encode the decade: S = 1970s, E = 1980s, N = 1990s, Z/DZ = 2000s, US = 2010s onward, with the first digit after the letter giving the specific year (e.g. S8XXXXX = 1978, N2XXXXXX = 1992). (Backed by **VG-0063**. Strong AEO target for "fender serial number S/E/N decode.")

4. **Q: Can I date a vintage Fender amplifier by its serial number?**
   A: Generally no — Fender kept no serial records for vintage amps, so the tube chart date code (and pot/transformer codes) is the reliable method, not the serial. (Backed by **VG-0052**. This also gives a natural contextual link to `/vintage-fender-amplifier-serial-numbers-how-to-find-the-year/` — the under-linked amp page.)

Adding 2-4 of these extends the existing `faqs` array (which already feeds `faqSchema`), so they inherit FAQPage markup automatically — no schema change needed.

### 8. DB fact check

Cross-checked every serial range, date, prefix, and value claim against the VG index. **No contradictions found** — the page is unusually clean and matches the DB facts closely. Details:

**Confirmed consistent with the DB:**
- Bridge→neck-plate transition ~1954: matches **VG-0066**. ✓
- L-series spanning 1963-1965 pre-CBS→CBS: matches **VG-0067**. ✓
- F-plate 1965-1976 (large "F" neck plate): matches **VG-0068**. ✓
- Blackguard = 1950 to mid-1954, black phenolic/Bakelite guard: matches **VG-0069**. ✓
- S/E/N headstock decade letters from 1976: matches **VG-0063** (page adds Z/DZ=2000s, US=2010s, consistent extension). ✓
- Mexican MN/MZ/MX = 1990s/2000s/2010s: matches **VG-0065** exactly. ✓
- MIJ vs CIJ reused letter prefixes (the two MIJ/CIJ tables share letters like A/B/O/P with different year ranges): matches the **VG-0064** warning that the prefixes are reused and must not be confused. ✓
- Pot codes: 304=Centralab, 137=CTS, 134=Stackpole: matches **VG-0047 / VG-0101**. 3-digit (year-digit+week) and 4-digit (2-digit-year+week) decode, "earliest possible date only": matches **VG-0054 / VG-0100 / VG-0102 / VG-0048 / VG-0099**. The worked example "304 6243 = Centralab week 43 of 1962" is internally correct. ✓
- Neck heel date = single most reliable method, applied by the worker: matches **VG-0051 / VG-0055**. ✓
- Serial overlap / "pre-stamped neck plates in batches / no reliable single-year dating before mid-1970s": matches **VG-0050 / VG-0053 / VG-0060 / VG-0061 / VG-0062 / VG-0111**. ✓
- Pre-CBS = before CBS Jan 1965: matches **VG-0049 / VG-0072**. ✓
- Custom colors from DuPont automotive paints, originals command a premium: matches **VG-0058 / VG-0073**; the page's "refinish reduces value" theme aligns with **VG-0074 / VG-0107**. ✓
- Slab (mid-1959 to mid-1962) → veneer rosewood transition; maple-only before mid-1959: matches **VG-0070** (page's "August 1962 is the magic month" is a finer-grained, plausible elaboration). ✓

**Minor note (NOT a contradiction — verify, don't flag):**
- §8 Custom Shop CZ row dates "Z = 2000s" for Custom Shop, while §9 lists `Z` (and the worked examples) also for standard US production 2000s — consistent. The page's "Z504999 = 2005" example: Z=2000s, first digit 5 → 2005, internally correct. ✓
- The CBS sale specifics on this page are framed only as "January 1965"; **VG-0059** has the precise "$13 million, January 5, 1965" and **VG-0072** the "completed early Jan 1965" nuance. The page does not contradict these; it just states the year. No fix needed.

**Solid facts ON this page that are MISSING from the DB — candidates to ADD** (the DB is light on Fender hardware/construction-dating tells; this page is a goldmine for them):

1. **Telecaster bridge saddles: brass (1950 to mid-1954) → steel (mid-1954 to 1958); brass ≈5/16" dia, steel ≈1/4".** (§12 Bridge Saddles.) Source: page §12 + measurable spec. Strong dating tell, no VG fact covers saddle material/diameter.
2. **Stratocaster saddles: stamped steel "FENDER PAT. PEND." (1954 to 1971) → die-cast zinc block saddles (late 1971+).** (§12.) Fast CBS-era visual ID; no VG fact.
3. **Kluson Deluxe tuner stamping sequence: No-Line (1950 to mid-1956) → Single-Line (mid-1956 to late 1964) → Double-Line (late 1964 to 1967); F-Style Schaller (chrome, "F" stamp) from ~1965/1968.** (§12 Tuner Evolution.) DB has Gibson Kluson stamps (VG-0019) but nothing Fender-specific; "PAT. APPLD." underside = pre-1954 is a clean addable fact.
4. **Fender logo evolution: Spaghetti (1950 to early 1964) → Transition gold-foil (mid-1964 to 1967) → CBS/TV heavy-black (1968 to 1980s).** (§12 Logo Evolution.) Pairs with VG-0071 (CBS visual tells in stages) but the named logo eras + dates aren't in the DB.
5. **Clay/fiberboard dots (1959 to late 1964) → pearloid dots (late 1964+); side dots switched to pearloid in EARLY 1964, before the main dots.** (§12 Fretboard Inlays.) The "early-1964 side-dots-first" detail is a sharp, citable transition tell absent from the DB.
6. **Pickguard chemistry: single-ply black Bakelite (Tele, 1950-1959) / cellulose-nitrate 3-ply "mint green" white-when-new (Strat, 1959 to late 1964) / stable white PVC (late 1964+).** (§12 Pickguards.) Ties to VG-0104 (nitro) but the pickguard-material-by-era mapping is new.
7. **Headstock back-stamp prefixes JD = "Japan Dyna" (2010s) and the CA/CB/CE limited CBS-era two-letter Gold-Strat/Bass/Tele prefixes.** (§9.) Niche but verifiable; not in the DB.
8. **V-prefix Vintage Reissue (1982+) carries NO year code — date by neck stamp/pot codes only.** (§7.) The DB covers L/F/headstock systems but not the V-reissue "no decode" caveat; worth adding as a "do not date by serial" fact alongside VG-0052 (amps).

Recommend adding #1-#5 as the highest-value Fender construction-dating facts (they are the cross-referencing spine the page's E-E-A-T is built on and are exactly the "what year is my Fender by hardware" content AI assistants ground on). Source attribution: Joe Dampt / Joe's Vintage Guitars fender-guitars-serial-number-guide (primary-expert authored).

  - Q: "How do I read an 8-digit Gibson serial number?" A: first + fifth digits = last two digits of the year; digits 2–4 = day of the year (YDDDYRRR). **VG-0035** (and VG-0016 for the plant-rank detail).
  - Q: "Why does my Gibson serial start with 94 but isn't from 1994's normal sequence?" A: the 1994 Centennial exception (already in body copy; promote to FAQ).
- **Reused Number Era section** — no FAQ. Add:
  - Q: "Why does my 1960s Gibson serial number match more than one year?" A: 1961–1969 numbers were duplicated/reused; serial alone can't date them — confirm by physical features + pot codes. **VG-0011 / VG-0013 / VG-0031 / VG-0032 / VG-0036** (cite 100000–106099 = 1963 or 1967).
  - Q: "Can a pot code date a 1960s Gibson?" A: it gives only the earliest-possible build date (no-earlier-than). **VG-0099 / VG-0100 / VG-0102**.
- **Custom Shop / Historic Reissue section** — no FAQ. The two existing top-of-page FAQ-schema Qs (Custom Shop CS prefix, Les Paul Classic) are in JSON-LD but NOT rendered as visible accordions — recommend surfacing them as visible Q/A here so schema and on-page match (avoids "FAQ markup not visible on page" Rich-Results risk).
- **FON section** — well covered in-body but no FAQ. Optional Q: "What's the difference between a Gibson FON and a serial number?" A: FON = internal batch number ink-stamped on bare wood, used ~1902–1961, often assigned before completion (so a 1959 ES-335 can carry a 1958 FON). **VG-0012 / VG-0039**.

### 8. DB fact check

**No contradictions with the DB found — the serial/spec claims align with VG facts.** Spot-checks:
- 1961–69 reused/overlapping numbers, "serial alone can't date" → matches **VG-0011/0013/0031/0032/0036/0111**. The body's "100,000 to 106,099 = 1963 or 1967" row matches VG-0036 exactly. ✅
- FON suffix A=1935…H=1942 → matches **VG-0034**. ✅
- Modern 8-digit YDDDYRRR (digits 1+5 = year, 2–4 = day) → matches **VG-0035**; Kalamazoo-low / Nashville-high plant note → **VG-0016**. ✅
- Volute appears ~1969–70, Norlin-era marker → matches **VG-0008/0010/0046**; Norlin 1969–1986 (page says Norlin "era" 1969–1984 for the *ownership/serial* window, then names the 1986 sale of the company elsewhere) → consistent with **VG-0023** (Norlin 1969–1986). Minor framing nuance, not an error: the page dates the **ownership** sale to 1984 and Norlin *name/era* through 1986-ish; VG-0023 uses 1969–1986. **Recommend a one-line reconciliation** so the page's "1969 to 1984" header and VG-0023's "1969–1986" don't read as conflicting (the 1984/1986 gap = sale agreement vs. completion). Low severity.
- "Made in USA" stamp from 1970 onward → matches **VG-0007**. ✅
- PAF = Patent Applied For, Seth Lover, intro 1957, → ~1962 patent-number changeover; patent no. 2,737,842 is NOT the humbucker patent → page correctly states the changeover but does **not** repeat the "wrong-patent" trivia. Matches **VG-0003 / VG-0024 / VG-0026**. ✅
- PAF DC resistance "7.5k–8.5k, varies, inconsistency is itself authentic" → matches **VG-0027**. ✅
- ES-335 dot→block inlay change "late 1962" → matches **VG-0045**. ✅
- Burst Standard 1958–1960, "fewer than 1,500 produced," "~643 sunburst shipped in 1959," prices "exceed $500,000" → consistent with **VG-0028 (≈1,700 made), VG-0029 (≈1,500–1,700 survive), VG-0030 (mid-1958–1960 only), VG-0028 ($200k–500k+)**. The page's "fewer than 1,500" (FAQ #07) leans to the survival figure and "643 in 1959" is a per-year subset — both compatible with VG-0028/0029, no contradiction. ✅

**Facts on this page MISSING from the DB — recommend adding (with the page as source, Joe-authored):**

- **VG-NEW (Gibson FON suffix/prefix split):** Gibson FONs used a **trailing** letter for year 1935–1942 (A–H) but a **leading** prefix letter for year 1952–1961 (Z=1952 … Q=1961). The DB has the 1935–42 suffix (VG-0034) but NOT the 1952–61 *prefix* (Z–Q) mapping. Add it. Source: page FON prefix table.
- **VG-NEW (FON-vs-serial year gap):** a Gibson FON is assigned when a batch *enters* production, so a guitar can carry a FON one year earlier than its serial — e.g. a 1959 ES-335 with a 1958 FON. Extends VG-0012/0039. Source: page "Real World Example" callout.
- **VG-NEW (1994 Centennial exception):** for most of 1994 Gibson abandoned the split-digit system and began every serial with "94"; confirm via 100th-anniversary 12th-fret banner inlay / headstock coin. Not in DB. Source: page modern-system warn callout.
- **VG-NEW (2010s year-stamp exception):** in a brief 2010s window Gibson stamped the literal 4-digit year of manufacture below "MADE IN USA," overriding the split-digit decode. Not in DB. Source: page modern-system callout.
- **VG-NEW (Les Paul Classic serial format):** Classic used an ink-stamp serial 1989–2014 — 1 year-digit (1989–99) vs 2 year-digits (2000–14), no "Made in USA" on the core model; only the 2007 Classic *offshoots* (Antique/Custom/GotW) used the modern 9-digit impressed serial + MIUSA stamp. Not in DB; useful authentication fact. Source: page Les Paul Classic section.
- **VG-NEW (Historic Reissue R-number serial):** Historic Reissue Les Pauls (R4/R7/R8/R9/R0) ink-stamp serial = first digit is the *reissued vintage year* (9 = 1959 reissue), second digit = last digit of *actual* build year, rest = rank. Not in DB. Source: page Custom Shop/Reissue section.
- **VG-NEW (ES-330 vs ES-335 tells):** ES-330 = fully hollow (no center block), P-90s, 16th-fret neck joint pre-1968; the 1968+ ES-330L "long neck" moved the joint to the 19th fret like the 335. Useful model-ID fact, not in DB. Source: page ES-330 section.
- **VG-NEW (ES-335 cutaway dating):** rounded "Mickey Mouse ear" horns = 1958–1961, pointed horns = 1962+. Complements VG-0045 (dot→block). Source: page ES-335 cutaway section.

### 3. FAQ gaps

The page has a 5-Q FAQ at the bottom but no section-level FAQs. Two gaps where a short Q/A would help, plus 2 additions to the existing FAQ:

- **§8.5 Timeline / rosewood section** lacks an FAQ. Suggested Q/As:
  - **Q: When did Martin switch from Brazilian to Indian rosewood?** A: Martin switched from Brazilian rosewood to East Indian rosewood on its rosewood-body models in **1969** (the change ran into 1970), driven by supply shortages — not CITES. **(VG-0088, VG-0089, VG-0109)**
  - **Q: When did Martin stop scalloping its braces?** A: Martin phased out scalloped top bracing in **late 1944**, switching to heavier non-scalloped (tapered) bracing; this is the line collectors use to define "pre-war." **(VG-0086, VG-0079)**
- **§4 Range chart** could carry one inline FAQ:
  - **Q: What was the last serial number Martin issued in 1898?** A: **8348** — the last serial of the series' first year. **(VG-0083)** (Note: the page's own guitar table shows 1898 ending at 8348, so this is consistent — see DB check below.)
- **Existing FAQ additions:**
  - **Q: Does the serial number alone date a Martin?** A: Yes for guitars — Martin has used one continuous, sequential serial series since 1898, so the number alone identifies the year. Mandolins, ukuleles, and Little Martin LX models use separate sequences. **(VG-0082)**
  - **Q: Where exactly is the serial number stamped?** A: On flat-tops it is stamped on the neck block inside the body, visible through the soundhole; the size/style number was added above it starting **October 1930**. **(VG-0077, VG-0078)** (This overlaps the existing "Where is the serial number" FAQ — fold the Oct-1930 detail in rather than adding a duplicate Q.)

- **VG-NEW (Martin mandolins): "Martin ceased mandolin production in 2002; mandolins were custom-order only 1994–2002; from serial 509,122 (1991) the mandolin sequence merged into the standard guitar serial sequence."** Source: §6 + the tool's per-type note. Specific, datable, and not in the DB.
- **VG-NEW (Martin): "Gold decal logo introduced 1932; before 1932 the brand was stamped on the back of the headstock, not the front."** Source: §8.4. A datable logo-evolution tell absent from the DB.

These are solid, sourced-on-page facts that fit the Martin KB; recommend Josh verify and add them (especially the 1934 T-fret and 1916 Ditson dreadnought items — high dating value).

### 3. FAQ gaps

The page has **no visible FAQ section** (the original FAQPage JSON-LD was deliberately removed per the page header comment because the 10 Q&A were never rendered). Given GSC queries (*dating rickenbacker guitars*, *how to date a rickenbacker guitar*) and the page's depth, a SHORT visible FAQ (3–4 Q&A, rendered, with matching FAQPage schema) near the bottom would capture long-tail and is worth adding. Suggested Q&A drawn from the page's own content:

- **Q: How do I find the serial number on a Rickenbacker?** A: On most Ricks from 1961 onward it is stamped on the output jackplate (letters above the jack hole, digits below). Some 1960s lower-end Combo solidbodies kept the serial on the bridge plate; the vibrato-equipped Combo 425 (1965–1967) stamped it on the vibrato housing. (From the page's jackplate/bridge-stamp + 425 edge-case sections — no DB fact needed.)
- **Q: What year is my Rickenbacker if the serial starts with two letters?** A: Two-letter serials are the 1961–1986 system: the first letter is the year (A=1961 … Z=1986) and the second is the month (A=January … L=December). Example: GD = July… (correction: G=1967, D=April → April 1967). Cross-check VG-0094.
- **Q: My Rickenbacker serial starts with XX — what does that mean?** A: XX has no dating value. It identifies a 1980s replacement service jackplate, stamped that way to keep them off counterfeit instruments. (From the page's "XX Replacement Jackplates" section.)
- **Q: Can a Rickenbacker be dated without a serial number?** A: Yes — pickups, knobs, tuners, inlays, body style, and tailpiece all changed on documented timelines; triangulate three or more features. (From the Advanced Dating sections.)

Mark for verification: the two-letter year/month answer should be cross-checked against **VG-0094** (confirms the 1961–1986 two-letter jackplate code, first letter = year). No other answer needs a DB fact.

### 8. DB fact check

Cross-checked the page's factual claims against the DB index (VG-0001..VG-0112). Only one Rickenbacker fact exists in the DB:

- **VG-0094** [Rickenbacker]: "Rickenbacker used a two-letter date code (typically on the jackplate) from 1961 to 1986: the first letter is the [year]…" — **CONFIRMS** the page's "Era Guide: 1961 to 1986 (Two-Letter Code)" section and the year/month letter grids (A=1961…Z=1986, second letter = month). **No contradiction.** The page is consistent with the DB.

**No WRONG / contradicting claims found** against the DB. (The page's other claims — Combo year-digit key, JK/JL Nov–Dec 1960 window, 1987–1998 letter+digit swap, 1999+ year+week format, XX replacement plates, Hi-Gain/Toaster/Horseshoe timelines, Kluson closure 1981/1982, R-tailpiece brass-vs-Zamak, triangle-inlay evolution — are not covered by any VG fact, so nothing to flag as contradicting. They appear internally consistent and match well-established Rickenbacker reference data.)

**Solid facts on this page MISSING from the DB — recommend adding** (this page is by far the richest Rickenbacker source in the project; the DB has only VG-0094 for the brand):

1. **1999–present year+week serial format:** YY+WW+sequence; first two digits = year (99=1999, 00=2000 … 26=2026), next two = production week 01–52(53). *Source: this page, "Era Guide: 1999 to Present."* Strong, decodable, high-query.
2. **1987–1998 letter+digit serials (letter=month, digit=year), with the A–L block (1987–1996, base year 1987) and the M–Y-skip-O block (1997–1998).** *Source: this page, "Era Guide: 1987 to 1998."*
3. **XX-prefix = 1980s replacement service jackplate, no dating value.** *Source: this page, "XX Replacement Jackplates."* Useful counterfeit/anti-fraud fact.
4. **Pre-1961 Rickenbacker serials are NOT reliably date-decodable** (model/config info only; year digit disappears late 1958); date these by spec. *Source: this page, pre-1961 era guide + "Pre-1961 Numbers Without Date Information."* Mirrors the Fender/Gibson "serial ≠ exact year" guardrail facts (VG-0050, VG-0011) — worth a parallel Rickenbacker fact.
5. **Headstock spelling tell:** "Rickenbacher" (with H) = pre-1950 (Adolph Rickenbacher era); "Rickenbacker" (with K) = 1950+ (F.C. Hall ownership). *Source: this page, "Headstock Logo and Spelling."* Clean binary dating cue.
6. **Serial reflects jackplate STAMP date, not always the instrument's finish date** (can differ by days/weeks/rarely months). *Source: this page, "A note on accuracy" callout.* The honesty guardrail for Rickenbacker, parallel to VG-0048/VG-0053 for components/Fender.

These six are well-sourced (the page itself, which reads as expert reference material) and would lift the brand from 1 → ~7 verified Rickenbacker facts, feeding the Dataset descriptions in §7 and the FAQ in §3.

### 3. FAQ gaps

The page already has a 5-question FAQ (read Guild SN / serial location / dating without serial / Westerly Guild / value). That's solid coverage of the head queries. Genuine gaps where an added Q/A would help, drawn from the page's own topic and the gsc.md query set ("guild serial number chart," "vintage guild serial numbers lookup"):

- **Q: "What do the letter prefixes on a Guild serial number mean?"**
  A: From 1965 to 1969 and again from 1979 through 1996, the letter prefix identifies the *model*, not the year — the digits give the year within that model's run. The same number can mean different things on different models, so you must find your model in the era charts above. (Mirrors the page's own "Heads-up" disclaimer; closes the "model-specific prefix" query gap. No DB fact needed — VG-0093 supports the pre-1965 single-sequence framing.)
- **Q: "How do I read a modern Guild serial number with two letters and six digits?"**
  A: For Tacoma (from Feb 2005) and New Hartford (from Dec 2008) Guilds, the first letter is the plant (T or N), the second letter is the year (I=2005 … N=2010), the next three digits are the day of the year, and the last three are that day's unit number. Example: TJ 037 016. (Restates the page's Part 8 Julian list as a quick-answer FAQ; high "modern guild serial" intent. **Needs DB add** — see section 8; no VG-#### covers Guild Julian codes yet.)
- **Q: "Are Guild serial numbers a reliable way to date the guitar?"**
  A: They get you the era, but a worn or replaced part can mislead — confirm with physical features (labels, pot/EIA codes, hardware) just as you would on any vintage instrument. (Parallels the honesty caveat the DB carries for Fender/Gibson — VG-0050, VG-0011 — applied to Guild. Reinforces E-E-A-T and matches the page's existing authentication checklist.)

The existing 5 FAQs are good; suggest adding 2–3 of the above rather than rewriting any.

From 1965 to 1969, a separate serial system was introduced for each model." → **matches VG-0093** ("Guild used a single continuous sequential serial number sequence across all models through 1964"). ✓

The page's Part 2 is titled "The Westerly Era (1970 to 1979)" and Parts 4–7 extend Westerly serialization into the 1980s–1990s, which is consistent with a 1966–2001 factory life. Suggested as a sibling to VG-0093.
2. **Guild modern Julian serial system (2005+).** Claim: two letters + six digits (e.g. TJ 037 016); first letter = plant (T=Tacoma, N=New Hartford), second letter = year (I=2005, J=2006, K=2007, L=2008, M=2009, N=2010), next three digits = day of year (001–365), last three = unit of the day. Tacoma from Feb 2005, New Hartford from Dec 2008. **No VG-#### covers this** — high-value add (it's the format modern buyers search and the FAQ in section 3 depends on it). Verify the year-letter mapping (I=2005…) against a primary Guild source before adding.

### 3. FAQ gaps

The page has a 6-Q FAQPage accordion at the bottom but several mid-page sections that draw their own search demand have no inline FAQ. Suggested additions (Q/A drawn from the page's own copy; VG-#### where a DB fact backs the answer):

- **In `#gretsch-serial-numbers-2003-present` (Fender era) — no FAQ.** Q: "What does a JT serial number mean on a Gretsch?" A: JT = Japan, Terada factory (Professional Series); next two digits = year, next two = month, final four = that factory's unit number for the year, e.g. JT03074463 = July 2003. (Page's own prefix table.)
- **In `#gretsch-pickup-dating` — no FAQ.** Q: "How do I tell a Filter'Tron from a HiLo'Tron?" A: They share a humbucker-sized cover, but a HiLo'Tron holds a single lightly-wound coil (~2–3K, lower output) while a Filter'Tron is a true dual-coil humbucker. (Page copy.) Q: "What year did Gretsch start using Filter'Trons?" A: Filter'Trons debuted at the 1957 NAMM show and rolled into production 1957–58 — note this was technically the first humbucking design into production, alongside Gibson's PAF (cross-checks VG-0091 era; no direct VG for Filter'Tron debut — flag for DB add, see §8).
- **In `#gretsch-serial-numbers-1939-1966` — no FAQ.** Q: "My Gretsch has a serial between 21,000 and 26,000 — is it a 1957?" A: Maybe, but check pickups and inlays first: ~1,000 1957-range labels were misplaced and reused in 1965, so a guitar in that range with HiLo'Trons or a double cutaway is a 1965, not a 1957. (Page's 1957/1965 anomaly callout.)
- **In `#gretsch-serial-numbers-1966-1972` — no FAQ.** Q: "Why can't my date-coded Gretsch serial be pinned to one year?" A: October/November/December 1969 codes (10/11/12) collide with January 1970/71/72; only physical features resolve it (VG-0092 confirms this two-digit-month ambiguity).

These can stay as the existing bottom accordion (don't fragment FAQPage schema) but the **Fender-prefix Q and the Filter'Tron-vs-HiLo'Tron Q are genuinely missing** and have search demand ("what does JT mean gretsch serial", "filtertron vs hilotron") — worth adding to the bottom FAQ array (and the FAQPage JSON-LD) rather than new mid-page accordions.

5. **Fender-era 2-letter factory prefixes** (JT=Japan/Terada, CY=China/Yako, CS=USA Custom Shop, KS=Korea/Samick, etc.) — the modern Gretsch decode key; analogous to the Fender MN/MZ/MX and Gibson YDDDYRRR facts already in the DB (VG-0065, VG-0035).

### 3. FAQ gaps

The page has **no FAQ section and no FAQPage JSON-LD** at all — a real gap for an Archetype-B reference page (every other serial guide on the site carries FAQ schema, per CLAUDE.md). The questions below mirror real "fender amp serial" search intent (gsc) and would earn FAQPage rich-result eligibility. Add as a collapsible accordion before §tc-10, with FAQPage JSON-LD.

- **Q: Can I date a vintage Fender amp by its serial number?** A: No — Fender amp serial numbers weren't sequential and Fender kept no serial-to-date records, so the serial alone won't give you a year. Use the tube-chart date code, then transformer/speaker codes and era features. *(Needs DB fact — cite **VG-0052**: "Fender amplifiers generally cannot be dated by serial number for vintage units because Fender kept no serial records.")*
- **Q: Where is the date code on a Fender amp?** A: It's the ink-stamped two-letter code on the paper tube chart glued inside the chassis (usually the left inner side). First letter = year (A=1951 … T=1970), second letter = month (A=January … L=December). *(Self-contained from §tc-2 + decoder; no DB fact needed.)*
- **Q: What if my Fender amp's tube chart is missing?** A: Date it by era appearance (Tweed 1948-1959, Blonde/Brownface 1959-1963, Blackface 1963-1967, Silverface 1967-1980) combined with the speaker or transformer codes, which give the last digit of the year. *(Self-contained from §tc-3–§tc-9.)*
- **Q: How do I read a Fender speaker code?** A: It's a 6-digit, numbers-only code: a 3-digit manufacturer (EIA) code, then 3 digits where the first gives the last digit of the year and the rest the week. Cross-reference the era to resolve the decade (a "5" is 1955, 1965, or 1975). *(Self-contained from §tc-9. NOTE for the writer: the page calls this a "3 digit manufacturer code"; the EIA source-date system in **VG-0047 / VG-0101** is a real cross-reference if you want to name CTS=137 / CentraLab=134 / Stackpole=304, but keep the FAQ answer simple.)*

### 8. DB fact check

Cross-checked the page's factual claims against VG-0001…VG-0112.

**Claims that CHECK OUT (consistent with DB):**
- §tc-1: "Fender amp serial numbers are not useful for finding their year… weren't always sequential." ✅ Matches **VG-0052** ("Fender amplifiers generally cannot be dated by serial number for vintage units because Fender kept no serial records"). Solid; this is the page's thesis and the DB backs it.
- §tc-2 tube-chart table: A=1951 through T=1970, first letter = year, second = month. ✅ Consistent with **VG-0052** (tube chart is the method). The letter-year mapping is the standard accepted Fender tube-chart code; no contradicting VG fact.
- §tc-9: speaker/transformer codes = 3-digit manufacturer (EIA) code + year/week digits, giving only the last digit of the year. ✅ Aligns with **VG-0047** (EIA prefixes 134/137/304), **VG-0048 / VG-0100** (EIA codes give only the EARLIEST possible build date), and **VG-0102** (digits after the maker code = year then week). The page's "first number… indicates the last number in the year of manufacture" is correct for the single-digit-year speaker stamp.

**Potential WEAKNESS to flag (not a hard contradiction):**
- §tc-9 frames the speaker/transformer code as giving a usable build year once you cross-reference the era. The DB's **VG-0048 / VG-0100** stress that an EIA source-date code establishes only the **earliest possible** build date (the component could have sat in inventory before assembly). The page doesn't carry this "no earlier than" caveat for amps. **Recommendation:** add a one-line caveat (mirrors the honesty guardrail used on the guitar guides) — "a component code tells you the amp is no *older* than that date, not its exact build date." Low severity; improves accuracy + AEO trust.
- §tc-10: "sell your amplifier made before 1967" vs §tc-1's scope note "vintage Fender amps made in 1980 & before" vs the table running to T=1970 and Silverface era to 1980. The "before 1967" cutoff in the sell CTA is a **buying-preference statement** (what Joe wants to buy), not a dating fact, so it doesn't contradict the dating ranges — but a reader could read it as a dating boundary. Minor copy clarity only; no DB conflict.

**Solid facts on this page MISSING from the DB — recommend adding:**
- **NEW FACT candidate (tube-chart code system):** "Vintage Fender amplifiers (through ~1970) carry an ink-stamped two-letter date code on the paper tube chart inside the chassis: the first letter encodes the year (A=1951 … T=1970) and the second letter the month (A=January … L=December)." The DB has VG-0052 (amps not serial-datable) but **no entry for the actual tube-chart letter-code key** — the positive dating method. This is the single most reusable amp-dating fact on the site and belongs in the DB. Source: this page + standard Fender amp field references.
- **NEW FACT candidate (Fender amp cosmetic eras):** "Vintage Fender amp covering eras: Tweed 1948-1959, Blonde & Brownface 1959-1963, Blackface 1963-1967, Silverface 1967-1980 — used to bracket a build-year range when the tube chart is missing." No amp-era VG fact exists (the DB's era facts are all Gibson/Fender *guitar* construction). Worth adding as the visual-dating companion to the tube-chart fact. Source: §tc-3–§tc-8 of this page.
- **NEW FACT candidate (speaker code year digit):** "On a vintage Fender speaker/transformer code (6 digits, numbers only), the first digit after the 3-digit EIA manufacturer code gives the last digit of the year; resolve the decade by the amp's cosmetic era." Partially covered by VG-0102 generically, but the **amp-specific application** (resolve decade via Tweed/Blonde/Blackface/Silverface) is not in the DB. Source: §tc-9.

### 3. FAQ gaps

The page has a 6-Q FAQPage (good, schema-backed). Sections that lack their own FAQ where one would help:

**A. Condition Grading section** (currently 0 FAQ). Suggested Q/A, drawn from the page's own tables:
- Q: "What's the difference between Very Good and Very Good+ on a vintage guitar?" — A: from the table copy: VG+ = honest player wear, moderate checking, all-original hardware, original/good-refret (60-75% of mint); VG = visible wear, heavier checking, minor part replacements, plays well after setup (45-60% of mint).
- Q: "How much does a refret or neck reset hurt value?" — A: routine maintenance, NOT originality-destroying; a refret is expected on a played vintage instrument. **VG-0110** (refret is routine maintenance, not a value-killer) and **VG-0107** (refinish is the real penalty) — distinguish refret from refinish in the answer.
- Q: "Does a repaired crack make an acoustic worthless?" — A: no; one neatly-repaired crack is acceptable at Very Good+ per the acoustic table; structural integrity + originality of the top matter more (**VG-0112** originality is the dominant driver).

**B. Collection Appraisals section** (currently 0 FAQ). Suggested:
- Q: "How big a collection will you appraise?" — A: page states largest single appraisal/purchase was **713 guitars and amps**; dozens of 100+ piece collections handled.

### 8. DB fact check

Cross-checked every factual claim on the page against VG-0001..VG-0112. **No contradictions found — the page is factually clean.** Claims that are SUPPORTED, plus facts the page asserts that are MISSING from the DB and worth adding:

**Supported / consistent with DB:**
- Refinish on golden-era Fender/Gibson "cuts collector value by about half" (FAQ, line 19) — consistent with **VG-0074** (refin ≈ −40% avg on Fender, more for desirable models) and **VG-0107** (refin = non-original finish penalty). The page's "about half" is the high end of VG-0074's range; defensible, not wrong.
- "Custom color Fender guitars are often worth twice as much (or more) than sunburst" (Case 1, line 76) — consistent with **VG-0073** (original custom-color commands ~40%+ premium; "twice as much" is within the documented range for desirable colors) and **VG-0058** (custom color = non-standard DuPont finish). OK.
- 1962 ES-335 "transition year," PAF vs early Patent-Number pickups, no-wire ABR-1, short-seam aluminum stop tailpiece (Case 2) — consistent with **VG-0045** (335 dot→block + pickup transition during 1962), **VG-0003/0024** (PAF vs patent-number ~1962-65), **VG-0043** (PAF magnet/spec transition). Accurate.
- Untouched solder joints / paint-stick marks / neck-heel date as Fender authentication (Case 1) — consistent with **VG-0051/0055** (neck-date is the most reliable Fender dating clue) and **VG-0058** (custom-color authentication). Accurate.
- Blacklight test for nitro "green glow" + its limits (Case 3) — consistent with **VG-0017** (aged nitro fluoresces greenish/yellowish) and **VG-0018** (blacklight blind spots). Accurate and appropriately caveated.
- "Originality is everything" theme throughout — aligns with **VG-0112** and **VG-0106** (all-original definition). Good.
- Market Pulse "asking prices vs actual sales data" — aligns with **VG-0108** (Reverb price guide = completed sales, asking prices are not values). Good.

**Solid facts ON this page that are MISSING from the DB — recommend adding:**
1. **Headstock break / repair value impact ≈ 40-50%** (FAQ, line 19: "A headstock break does about the same, usually 40% to 50%"). The DB has refinish penalties (VG-0074) but **no fact on headstock-break value impact**. Add: *"A repaired headstock break on a vintage Gibson/Fender typically reduces value by ~40-50%, similar to a refinish; the instrument remains saleable as player-grade."* Source visible on page (Joe's FAQ). High reuse value across sell/appraisal pages.
2. **Natural-finish Gibson ES-5 ≈ 3-4× rarer than Sunburst** (Case 3 outcome, line 98, "According to the Gibson shipping totals"). DB has Gibson shipping-totals facts for Les Paul Bursts (VG-0028/0029/0030) but **nothing on ES-5 natural vs sunburst rarity**. Add as a Gibson shipping-totals datapoint, sourced to the page's `/post/gibson-shipping-totals-1948-1979/` cluster.
3. **Gibson ES-5 "N" (Natural) label designation + missing-N as a factory slip** (Case 3, lines 96-98). DB covers Gibson labels broadly (VG-0038) but not the "N"-suffix-for-Natural convention. Add: *"Gibson appended 'N' to the label/model designation on Natural-finish instruments; absence of the 'N' on a genuine natural finish can be a factory slip rather than a red flag."* Useful Gibson-authentication fact.
4. **Refret is routine, not a value-killer (vs refinish)** is in DB (**VG-0110**) — but the page's electric/acoustic grading tables operationalize it (refret acceptable at VG+/VG). No new fact needed; flagged only to confirm the grading copy does NOT contradict VG-0110/VG-0107.

### 8. DB fact check

Cross-checked every factual claim on the page against VG-0001..VG-0112. **No contradictions found** — the page is conservative and consistent with the DB. Details:

**Claims that CHECK OUT against the DB:**
- "Pre-CBS Stratocaster," "collectible CBS-era" framing → consistent with VG-0049 / VG-0059 / VG-0072 (Pre-CBS = before CBS purchase finalized Jan 1965).
- Form dropdown serial ranges: "4-5 digits on BRIDGE plate (1950–1954)" → VG-0066 (early-'50s serials on bridge/cup plate, moved to neck plate ~1954). "L on NECK plate (1963–1965)" → VG-0067 (L-series ~1963–1965, final pre-CBS). "6-digit neck plate w/ large F (1965–1976)" → VG-0068 (F-plate Q3 1965–1976). "Letter prefix on headstock (1977–present)" → VG-0063 (1976+ headstock decal, S/E/N decade letters). "V prefix … reissue" and "Made in Japan and Mexico" → consistent with VG-0064 (JV/MIJ/CIJ) and VG-0065 (Mexico M-prefix). The form's *one-year-off* boundary ("1977–present" vs DB "1976+") is a UX simplification, not an error.
- "neck dates, pot codes, and hardware specs" as the real dating method → matches VG-0051/VG-0055 (neck date most reliable), VG-0054/VG-0099/VG-0100 (pot codes = "no earlier than" clue). The page wisely does NOT claim the serial alone dates the guitar — aligned with VG-0050/VG-0060/VG-0061.
- "Dakota Red finish and factory gold hardware were original, and those Pre-CBS 'Custom Color' features are rare and bring a real premium" (Mary's '63 Strat) → matches VG-0058 (custom color = non-standard DuPont automotive finish) and VG-0073 (original custom-color commands ~40%+ premium). **Dakota Red is a genuine Fender custom color** (DuPont code), so the claim is sound.
- "it still has value" for modified/refretted guitars → consistent with VG-0074 (refin ~−40%, not zero), VG-0110 (refret is routine), VG-0112 (originality is the dominant but not sole driver).

**Solid facts on the page MISSING from the DB (candidates to add):**
1. **"Dakota Red" is a documented Fender custom color** (DuPont automotive paint), and **factory gold hardware** was an available custom-order option on early-'60s Strats. Source visible on-page: the case-study copy; corroborate against the standard Fender custom-color chart.
2. **Model nicknames used on-page**: "Blackguard" Tele (already in DB as VG-0069), "No-caster"/"Broadcaster" (Telecaster pre-Broadcaster-trademark naming), and "Competition" finish Mustangs. *Suggested add:* a VG fact for the Broadcaster → No-caster → Telecaster naming sequence (1950–1951, Gretsch "Broadkaster" trademark conflict). The page asserts "Broadcasters, and No-casters" as buyable models; that lineage is a clean, citable dating fact not currently in the DB.

Neither gap is a correction — both are *additions* that would strengthen the Fender value/dating coverage. No claim on the page needs to be fixed.

### 3. FAQ gaps

The page already has a strong 8-Q FAQ (§12, 5 schema-tracked). Gaps where a Q/A would help, by section:

- **Best Way To Sell (§6)** lacks any FAQ on the selling-channel decision it raises. Suggested:
  - Q: "Should I sell my vintage Gibson on Reverb or to a private buyer?" A: covers the page's own point — Reverb has good shipping protection but charges fees and tends to side with buyers in disputes, while a direct cash sale removes the liability of shipping a high-value instrument. (Page-sourced; no DB fact needed.)
  - Q: "Is it risky to ship an expensive vintage guitar myself?" A: yes for a first-time seller above ~$4,000; most dealers carry $100k+ in shipment insurance, which is why Joe arranges prepaid, fully-insured labels. (Page-sourced.)
- **How Much Is My Gibson Worth (§5)** — add a value-driver FAQ tied to a DB fact:
  - Q: "Does refinishing or modifying my Gibson lower its value?" A: originality is the single largest value driver — an all-original guitar outranks a refinished or modified one (**VG-0112**, **VG-0106**, **VG-0107**); a refin typically costs ~40–50% (the existing FAQ Q6 already states ~50% for headstock repair/refin — keep consistent).
  - Q: "Can a serial number tell me exactly what year my Gibson was made?" A: not by itself for 1961–1969 Gibsons — those serials were duplicated and reused, so the year is confirmed by physical features, not the number alone (**VG-0009**, **VG-0011**, **VG-0111**). Useful because the intro form asks sellers to classify their serial.
- **Payout grid / Les Paul card (§11)** — a "Burst" rarity FAQ would add E-E-A-T:
  - Q: "What makes a 1958–1960 Les Paul Standard 'Burst' so valuable?" A: only ~1,500–1,700 were made from mid-1958 to 1960, and clean originals sell in the $200k–$500k+ range (**VG-0028**, **VG-0029**, **VG-0030**). Mark answer as VG-cited.

No FAQ gap on the banner/CTA sections.

### 8. DB fact check

Cross-checked every factual claim on the page against VG-0001..VG-0112. Findings:

**Claims that CHECK OUT (consistent with DB):**
- §6: "Most dealers carry over $100,000 in insurance just for their shipments" — business/logistics claim, not in DB; plausible, no contradiction.
- §6: high-end threshold "$4,000 & up" — judgment call, no DB conflict.
- FAQ Q3: "Les Pauls and SGs from the '50s and '60s are in the highest demand" — consistent with VG-0021 (SG = renamed Les Paul for 1961) and the Burst rarity facts (VG-0028/0029/0030). OK.
- FAQ Q6: "a headstock crack or a full refinish usually drops the value about 50%" — consistent with the refin penalty facts. NOTE: **VG-0074** gives Fender refin at ~−40% average and **VG-0107** describes refins generally; the Les Paul value page cites refin ~−40 to −50% (VG-0074/0107 per dataset-schema.md). The page's "about 50%" for a *headstock crack OR full refin* is within the cited band but sits at the top of it — defensible as a combined-damage figure, not wrong. Keep the hedge "usually... about."
- FAQ Q8 / §10: leave the guitar in as-found condition, old nitrocellulose finish, patina — consistent with VG-0104 (nitro), VG-0017/0018 (aged nitro behavior). OK.
- Payout Les Paul card: "1950s Goldtops, Bursts, and Customs... original PAF-equipped Les Pauls" — consistent with VG-0003 (PAF), VG-0041 (PAFs fitted to Goldtop during 1957), VG-0044 (Sunburst Standard introduced ~mid-1958). OK.
- Payout SG card: "early 1960s SG Standards and Customs with sideways or Lyre vibrolas" — model/era detail, consistent with VG-0021 (SG shape for 1961). OK.
- Payout Explorer card: "vintage Korina Explorers and 1970s models... 'Modernistic' series" — accurate Gibson terminology, no DB conflict.
- Payout Firebird card: "reverse and non-reverse Firebird I, III, V, VII... original banjo tuners" — accurate Firebird detail, not in DB, no conflict.
- Payout Acoustic card: "pre-war J-45s, J-200s, and Advanced Jumbos... 'Banner' era acoustics" — "Banner" headstock = wartime era; consistent with the demo-video catalog (1943 J-45 Banner). VG-0012 references FON/banner-era labeling. OK.

**No claims FLAGGED as wrong or contradicting a VG fact.** The page is conservative — it avoids hard serial ranges, production counts, and dated price figures (which is the right posture for a conversion page).

**Facts on this page MISSING from the DB and worth ADDING** (each is a solid, sourced-on-page claim the DB doesn't yet capture):

1. **Gibson Korina "Modernistic" series (Flying V + Explorer) rarity/collectibility** — page asserts these are "rare" and "collectible" (Flying V + Explorer payout cards). The DB has nothing on the 1958–59 Korina Flying V/Explorer run (one of the rarest production Gibsons, a few hundred made). Recommend adding a VG fact: *"The original 1958–1959 Gibson Korina (limba wood) Flying V and Explorer were produced in tiny numbers (low hundreds), making them among the most collectible vintage Gibson electrics."* Source: standard Gibson history; verify exact shipping figures before committing a count.
2. **Gibson Firebird "reverse vs non-reverse" + banjo (steering-wheel) tuners** — page distinguishes reverse/non-reverse Firebird I/III/V/VII and "original banjo tuners" as a value premium. DB has no Firebird entry. Recommend a VG fact on the reverse-body (1963–65) vs non-reverse (1965–69) Firebird transition and the side-mounted banjo tuners as an originality tell. Source: page copy + standard Gibson reference; verify dates.
3. **Gibson Super 400 / L-5 / ES-355 as top-tier acquisition targets** — page names these explicitly (intro + ES card) as the "golden-era archtops" Joe most wants. DB covers ES-335/330/dot-neck (VG-0040, VG-0045) but has no Super 400 or L-5 archtop entry. Recommend a VG fact placing the Super 400 and L-5 as Gibson's premium pre-war/golden-era archtops. Source: page + L5-CES value guide post (4,170 impr) already on-site.

These are additive; none corrects an error. Verify production counts against a primary source before entering, per the DB's honesty guardrail.

- **Serial/dating gap.** Add: **"Where is the serial number on my Martin and what year is it?"** A: stamped on the neck block inside the body, visible through the soundhole; Martin's continuous sequential series since 1898 dates it. **Cite VG-0077** (serial on neck block, through soundhole) and **VG-0082** (one continuous sequential series since 1898). Link the answer to `/martin-serial-and-model-numbers/`.
- **Pre-war value gap (the FAQ mentions "pre-war" but never defines it).** Add: **"What makes a pre-war Martin so valuable?"** A: herringbone trim, scalloped (forward-shifted) bracing, Brazilian rosewood, and pre-1944 construction. **Cite VG-0079** (pre-war = pre-1944), **VG-0075** (herringbone), **VG-0076/VG-0084** (scalloped/forward-shifted bracing), **VG-0080** (herringbone scalloped D-28 among most valuable). This directly strengthens the §11 model-card claims.
- **Brazilian rosewood gap.** Add: **"Are Brazilian rosewood Martins worth more than later models?"** A: yes; Martin used Brazilian rosewood through 1969 then switched to East Indian rosewood (a supply shortage, not CITES). **Cite VG-0088/VG-0089** (switch in 1969) and **VG-0109** (the switch was supply, not CITES — important honesty point, the page/FAQ should not repeat the common CITES myth).

2-4 additions recommended; the shipping + serial questions are the highest-value (they also create natural inbound-link anchors to the serial guide and shipping page).

### 8. DB fact check

Cross-checked every factual claim on the page against the VG index. **No contradictions found** — the page is conservative (mostly model names + service claims, light on hard dates). Findings:

**Claims that are CONSISTENT with the DB (no change needed):**
- §2/§7/§11 "Pre-War and Golden Era D-18s," "scalloped bracing and Adirondack spruce tops," "pre-war Dreadnoughts" — consistent with **VG-0076** (scalloped bracing = most resonant pre-war), **VG-0079** (pre-war ≈ pre-1944), **VG-0084** (forward-shifted scalloped X-bracing).
- §11 D-28 card "Brazilian Rosewood models from the 1930s through the late '60s" — consistent with **VG-0088/VG-0089/VG-0109** (Brazilian rosewood standard through 1969). The "late '60s" wording is accurate (switch was 1969/1970). ✅ Good — does not repeat the CITES myth VG-0109 warns against.
- §11 D-28 "vintage herringbone D-28s" + §6/§11 high-trim claims — consistent with **VG-0075** (herringbone purfling, pre-war D-28) and **VG-0085/VG-0087** (herringbone discontinued 1947). Page doesn't assert a specific herringbone end-date, so no risk.
- §11 OM card "how rare the 1929 to 1933 era is" for Orchestra Models — historically accurate (OM production 1929-1933 before the 14-fret 000 absorbed it); not in the DB but not contradicted.
- §11 D-45 card "I know the original abalone pearl inlay and the rare early production numbers" — consistent with **VG-0081** (D-45 halted 1942, reintroduced 1968 → pre-war D-45s genuinely rare/low-production). No date asserted, so safe.
- §6 "high-end acoustic worth over $4,000" / §8 "top dollar" — value framing, no specific figure to check against VG price facts. Fine.

**Solid facts ON the page worth ADDING to the DB (currently missing):**
- **Martin OM (Orchestra Model) production ran ~1929-1933** (from §11 OM card "how rare the 1929 to 1933 era is"). The DB has D-28/D-18/D-45/herringbone/bracing/rosewood facts but **no OM-specific date fact**. Recommend a new VG entry: *"The Martin Orchestra Model (OM) was produced roughly 1929-1933 before the 14-fret 000 superseded it; original OMs from that window are highly sought after."* Source visible on-page (Joe's claim); corroborate against Martin archive before committing.
- **The 0-18/0-21/0-28 ("Single-0") and 00 ("Grand Concert") body-size naming + 12-fret vs 14-fret configurations** (§11 cards "early concert-sized guitars," "rare 12-fret and 14-fret configurations"). The DB has VG-0078 (size/style stamped on neck block from Oct 1930) but **no body-size taxonomy fact** (0 = Concert, 00 = Grand Concert, 000 = Auditorium, D = Dreadnought). Recommend adding a Martin body-size reference fact — it underpins claims on this page, the dreadnought value guide, and the Martin serial guide.

**No WRONG facts to flag.** The page is clean; its main DB-relevant risk (the Brazilian-rosewood/CITES myth, VG-0109) is correctly avoided.

### 3. FAQ gaps

Current FAQs are the 5 generic resale FAQs (price determination, consignment/trade, payment, shipping tax, warranty) shared across all sell-my-* pages — **zero Rickenbacker-specific Q's**. The page would benefit from 2-3 brand-targeted FAQs (also strengthens the FAQPage schema for Ricky queries). Suggested adds, drawn from the page's own topic:

- **Q: How do I tell what year my Rickenbacker was made?** A: From roughly 1961 to 1986, Rickenbacker used a two-letter date code, usually stamped on the jackplate: the first letter gives the year and the second the month. Send Joe a photo of the jackplate and he can date it for you. *(needs DB fact: **VG-0094**)* — this Q also creates a natural in-FAQ link to `/rickenbacker-serial-numbers/`.
- **Q: Do you buy Rickenbacker basses as well as guitars?** A: Yes. Rickenbacker basses like the 4001 and 4003 are some of the most sought-after, and Joe buys them for cash nationwide alongside the electric guitars and amps. *(no DB fact; from page copy — hero already says "guitars and basses," and the testimonials mention a 4003)*
- **Q: Will an older Rickenbacker with replaced parts still sell?** A: It can, but originality is the single largest driver of a vintage guitar's value, so an all-original example is worth more than one with swapped tuners, pickups, or a refinish. Joe will tell you honestly how mods affect your offer. *(needs DB fact: **VG-0112**, supporting **VG-0106/0107**)*
- **Q: Can you date a vintage Rickenbacker amp by its serial number?** A: Not reliably — like most vintage amps, Rickenbacker/Electro amps are dated by their components and pot codes rather than a serial. *(supporting **VG-0099/0100** for pot-code dating; Ricky-amp-specific dating is not in the DB — see §8)*

Recommend adding the first three; they're well-supported and on-topic. The amp-dating Q is optional and partly outruns the DB.

The existing 5 FAQs are all generic (pricing factors, consignment, payment, shipping tax, warranty) — none is National/Valco specific. The page's own topic (dating + identifying Nationals) is unanswered. Add 2 to 4 National-specific Q/A:

1. **Q: How do I date my vintage National or Valco-built guitar?** A: Valco-made instruments (National, Supro, Airline, Oahu and other house brands) generally encode the year of construction in the serial number rather than using a model-only system, so the serial is the starting point, confirmed by hardware and finish features. *(needs DB fact — VG-0095.)*
2. **Q: What's the difference between a pre-war National Resonator and a 1950s Valco-built National?** A: Pre-war Nationals are the metal/wood-body single-cone and tricone resonators built before WWII; the 1950s "Valco-built" Nationals are the post-war electric and resonator models made after National-Dobro became Valco. (Page copy already draws this distinction in the hero — turn it into an FAQ.)
3. **Q: Do you buy National tricones and single-cone resonators?** A: Yes — tricone, single-cone, wood-body and metal-body resonators, plus tenor and ukulele resonators, are all of interest. (Mirrors the three feature-grid photos: tricone, ukulele, wood sunburst.)
4. **Q: Will you appraise a National even if the serial number is faded or unreadable?** A: Yes — send detailed photos and any partial serial/model markings; a value can usually be reached from the model, hardware and condition alone. (Backed by review R-Victor on this very page about a faded National serial.)

### 3. FAQ gaps

The page HAS a 5-Q FAQ (`#faqs-collection`) but every question is generic single-guitar copy ("appraise MY guitar", "sell MY vintage guitar"). It has **no collection-specific or logistics questions** despite the whole page being about large multi-instrument buys. Suggested additions (collection/estate/logistics framing — matches the *guitar liquidation / estate sale* queries this page ranks for):

- **Q: How large a collection will you buy in one visit?** A: There's no upper limit — I've bought 700+ guitars and amps from a single retiring collector in one trip. For large collections I drive my own box truck or fly out and rent one on-site, with the goal of buying the entire collection in one visit and paying the same day. *(Backed by Notable Purchase #01 copy — no DB fact needed.)*
- **Q: Do you buy guitar collections from an estate or after a death in the family?** A: Yes. A lot of what I do is helping families and executors liquidate an inherited or estate collection. I'll appraise it remotely from photos first so there are no surprises, then come to you anywhere in the U.S. *(Targets "guitar estate sale" query directly.)*
- **Q: Will you buy amplifiers and other gear as part of the collection, not just guitars?** A: Absolutely — I buy basses, amplifiers, mandolins, banjos, and effects right alongside the guitars. One Southern Arizona buy was 100+ vintage Fender amps plus several guitars in a single day. *(Links naturally to /sell-an-amplifier-or-effect/.)*
- **Q: How do you decide what a whole collection is worth?** A: Each instrument is valued individually on make, model, year, condition, and originality, then totaled — **originality is the single biggest driver of a vintage instrument's value (VG-0112)**, so an all-original piece (VG-0106) is worth substantially more than a refinished one (VG-0107, ~−40% on average per VG-0074). Price-guide figures are estimates from completed sales, not firm quotes (VG-0108). *(Answer uses VG-0112 / VG-0106 / VG-0107 / VG-0074 / VG-0108 — cite when writing.)*

### 3. FAQ gaps

The page already has a solid 5-question FAQPage (types of amps, appraisal process, shipping, non-working amps, same-day pay). Gaps worth filling (2-4 suggested):

| Suggested Q | Suggested A | DB fact needed |
|---|---|---|
| **How Do You Date A Vintage Amp If The Serial Number Doesn't Work?** | "Most vintage Fender and similar amps can't be dated by serial number at all — the maker kept no serial-to-year records. The reliable method is the two-letter date code stamped on the tube chart inside the cabinet, plus EIA date codes on the transformers and speaker. Send me a photo of the tube chart and I'll date it." | **VG-0052** (amps not datable by serial; tube chart is the method). Also supports VG-0048/VG-0100 (EIA codes give "no earlier than" build date). This is the strongest FAQ to add — it's accurate, niche, and ties to the amp serial guide. |
| **Do You Buy Effects Pedals And Rack Units Too, Or Just Amps?** | "Both. Vintage and boutique effects — fuzz, overdrive, delay, modulation, rare studio rack units — are of real interest, especially early Boss, Electro-Harmonix, MXR, and one-off builds. | **Should I Have My Old Amp Serviced Or Re-Capped Before Selling?** | "No — sell it as-is. Original, un-serviced amps often carry more collector value, and I factor any needed work into a fair offer. A botched re-cap or non-original parts can actually lower value." | Mirrors the originality principle (VG-0106 all-original; VG-0112 originality is the dominant value driver). Useful, honest, conversion-friendly. |
| **What Information Helps You Make The Fastest Offer?** | "Brand and model, the tube-chart date code if visible, photos of the front, back, and chassis, and whether it's all-original or modified. With those I can usually give a fair-market value the same day." | Ties to VG-0052 (tube chart) and VG-0106 (all-original). Reinforces the appraisal CTA. |

### 3. FAQ gaps

The page has **no FAQ at all**, which is a miss for an Archetype A page (free-appraisal, sell-fender, sell-gibson all carry FAQPage JSON-LD). Add a `FAQPage`-marked accordion before ContactSection. Suggested Q/A drawn from the page's own topics:

1. **Q: How much does it cost to consign a guitar with Joe's Vintage Guitars?**
   A: Consignment fees start as low as 8% for top-tier vintage instruments, with no hidden or surprise charges. (Direct from the `why` array — verify the 8% figure is still current with Joe; not a DB fact.)
2. **Q: How long does consignment take, and is there a minimum period?**
   A: There is no minimum consignment period, and with an established buyer network a guitar sometimes sells almost immediately. You keep ownership until it sells.
3. **Q: Should I consign or sell my vintage guitar outright?**
   A: Consignment usually nets a higher final price because of professional marketing and a worldwide audience, but an outright sale is faster. Originality is the single largest driver of either number (**VG-0112**) — a refinished instrument can be worth a fraction of an all-original one (**VG-0074**: refinishing a vintage Fender reduces value by roughly 40% on average; **VG-0107**). Get a free valuation to compare. (Links to /sell-* pages + /free-appraisal/.)
4. **Q: How do you handle shipping and insurance once my guitar sells?**
   A: Joe handles full insurance and shipping and pays you by wire transfer, cash, check, or electronic transfer. (From the `steps` array; pair with the /jvg-shipping-process/ link.)

A FAQPage block also satisfies the same E-E-A-T/JSON-LD pattern used on the sibling conversion pages.

The page makes very few hard factual claims; most copy is service description. Cross-check:

- **"$100,000+ if it's original and around $13,000 if it's been refinished"** (Top-Dollar Sale → Authentication). This is a *directional* illustration, not a cited model figure. It is CONSISTENT with the DB direction: originality is the dominant value driver (**VG-0112**) and refinishing carries a large penalty (**VG-0074**: ~40% average reduction on vintage Fender; **VG-0107** refin definition; **VG-0073** original custom-color premium ~40%+). The specific $100k/$13k pair is not in the DB and is not contradicted by it — it reads as a rhetorical example. **No flag**, but if Joe wants it defensible, tie it to a specific model (e.g. a Burst, **VG-0028**: ~$200k–500k+) rather than leaving it generic.
- **"Consignment fees as low as 8%"** — business/pricing claim, not a verifiable vintage-guitar fact; out of DB scope. Verify currency with Joe before quoting in FAQ schema.
- **"a buyer network built over a decade" / "more than a decade selling correct instruments"** — biographical, not DB scope. Consistent with the site's E-E-A-T framing.

**No WRONG or contradicted facts found.**

**MISSING-from-DB candidates worth adding** (both are solid, on-page, and generalize beyond consignment):
1. *Claim:* "The same model can be worth $100,000+ original and ~$13,000 refinished." If Joe stands behind a concrete model example, add a VG fact capturing the magnitude of the refinish penalty on a high-end original (e.g. a specific Les Paul Burst or pre-CBS Strat), with Joe's own sales as source. 2. *Claim:* originality + documentation (receipts, original paperwork, original case/OHSC) materially raise value (Tips → "Document Its History"). The OHSC concept exists (**VG-0098**) but the broader "provenance/paperwork raises value" claim is not stated as its own fact — worth a short VG fact, sourced to Joe's consignment practice, since it recurs across sell/appraisal pages.
